learningObjective: Reason about the collectives that a partitioner must insert to reshard a tensor between two different sharding specifications on the same device mesh.

canonicalClaims.claim: Resharding from a per-rank-shard layout (each rank holds 1/N along an axis) to a per-rank-replicated layout (each rank holds the full tensor) is implemented by an AllGather along that axis; the reverse, from replicated to sharded, is a local slice with no collective.
conditions: The mesh axis and dimension being resharded are the same on both sides.
The tensor's element type is preserved through the reshard.
nonImplications: Does not imply that reshard cost is always AllGather; other pairs (partial → replicated) require AllReduce; (sharded axis X → sharded axis Y) requires All-to-All.
Does not imply that all reshards are cheap; large tensors resharded via AllGather move (N-1)/N · S per rank.

sourceMappings.locator: §3–§4 partitioner emits reshard collectives based on sharding specs

canonicalClaims.claim: Resharding from partial-sum (each rank holds a partially-reduced tensor to be summed) to fully replicated requires an AllReduce; to sharded requires a ReduceScatter.
conditions: The upstream op produced a 'partial' sharding annotation (e.g. after a matmul where the contracting axis was sharded).
nonImplications: Does not imply that partial-sum tensors are unusable; they are a valid intermediate sharding until the next consumer forces a reshard.

misconceptions.claim: Resharding from sharded to replicated always requires an AllReduce because every rank must end with the full tensor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Data was already partitioned (not partially summed); assembly across ranks requires AllGather, not AllReduce.

misconceptions.claim: Resharding between two sharded layouts along different axes (X-sharded → Y-sharded) can always be done as a local view / stride change with no communication.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Different sharding axes place different slices on different ranks; realigning them requires All-to-All (a permutation), not a local view.

misconceptions.claim: The compiler always inserts a single global collective at the graph boundary; individual op-to-op reshards do not exist.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Partitioners like GSPMD emit reshard collectives at any op boundary where the required input sharding differs from the produced sharding.
